forcedChoices.reason: The English uses 'seraphim' as a singular here ('an unknown seraphim'); Spanish needs the singular form 'serafín'.
The glossary gives the feminine form for the Mother Spirit; Spanish forces a gender on the article and noun.
Lutentia addresses Michael with archaic 'you' in a direct, formal declaration; 'tú' keeps the scriptural tone of 'Just and righteous are you in all your ways' without the distance of 'usted'.
Michael speaks to the Constellation Fathers as a group; Spanish requires a plural pronoun, and the packet requires 'ustedes'.
The English ordinal suffix 'st' has no Spanish match; the Spanish ordinal mark '.º' stays inside the existing <sup> tag.
Spanish puts the era abbreviation after the year; the scaps span stays with the abbreviation.
'reigned supreme' is an idiom; a literal 'reinó supremo' reads unnatural, so the plain sense of unchecked rule is kept.
'fellow creature' needs a gendered noun in Spanish; 'criatura' is feminine by grammar only and keeps the English sense.
